meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until twenty to five, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now, on what basis?
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A student misquotes Shakespeare, so that's your case? Show me the page in his essay where it appears. And what else do you have, Hale, or is that it?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.
You'll want to be very careful about your next sentence, Hale. "It seems to run in the family." I'm writing that down word for word, and the principal will be reading it this afternoon.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this matter be placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with nothing agreed and the principal now involved.
What moved her: "I should have called you before entering the zero," because it owned the process failure in one sentence without excuses and earned a flat okay.
What cost ground: "It seems to run in the family," because bringing up her daughter's case attacked the family instead of the work and sent her straight to the principal.
Try next time: right after raising the quoted line that isn't in Hamlet, show her the page of Owen's essay where it appears and give her a dated record of his process she can check, instead of turning to Claire.
